title: PostgreSQL Connection Pool Exhaustion
symptoms: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
SequelizeConnectionAcquireTimeoutError
psycopg2.OperationalError: server closed the connection unexpectedly
API p99 latency spike to >15s across all read/write endpoints
Active connections count hitting max_connections ceiling in Grafana/RDS
root_causes: Backend microservice instances scaled out rapidly without PgBouncer connection pooling
Long-running analytical queries blocking connection recycling
Unclosed transaction connections leaking in worker threads
diagnostic_commands: SELECT count(*), state, usename FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY state, usename;
SELECT pid, now() - query_start AS duration, query, state FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state != 'idle' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 10;
mitigation_steps: Terminate long-running uncommitted idle in transaction queries: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle in transaction' AND now() - query_start > interval '5 minutes';
Scale up PgBouncer pooler replicas or adjust max_client_conn in pgbouncer.ini
Rate-limit or pause asynchronous bulk-report cron jobs triggering large table scans
Temporarily increase max_connections if memory permits, followed by controlled rolling restart of pooler
long_term_fix: Enforce strict query timeout (statement_timeout = '15s') in application ORM and route all analytical workloads to read replicas.

title: PostgreSQL Deadlocks and Blocked Transactions
symptoms: ERROR: deadlock detected - Process X waits for ExclusiveLock
Database row-level lock wait queue spiking
Checkout and user update requests failing with 500 internal errors
High lock duration in pg_stat_database
root_causes: Concurrent update operations updating foreign key parent/child tables in non-uniform key order
Batch jobs acquiring table-level locks concurrently with user-facing transactional writes
diagnostic_commands: SELECT blocked_locks.pid AS blocked_pid, blocking_locks.pid AS blocking_pid, blocked_activity.query AS blocked_statement, blocking_activity.query AS current_statement_in_blocking_process FROM pg_catalog.pg_locks blocked_locks JOIN pg_catalog.pg_stat_activity blocked_activity ON blocked_activity.pid = blocked_locks.pid JOIN pg_catalog.pg_locks blocking_locks ON blocking_locks.locktype = blocked_locks.locktype JOIN pg_catalog.pg_stat_activity blocking_activity ON blocking_activity.pid = blocking_locks.pid WHERE NOT blocked_locks.granted;
mitigation_steps: Identify the blocking process PID and cancel the transaction: SELECT pg_cancel_backend(blocking_pid);
If unresponsive, terminate the blocking backend: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(blocking_pid);
Temporarily disable the offending batch background migration job
long_term_fix: Audit conflicting transactions to standardize lock ordering and add optimistic concurrency locking.

title: OAuth2 / JWT Signature Verification & JWKS Key Rotation Failure
symptoms: All authenticated API requests failing with HTTP 401 Unauthorized
JsonWebTokenError: invalid signature or invalid algorithm
Error: Unable to verify JWT against JWKS URI: https://auth.company.com/.well-known/jwks.json
Customer login sessions invalidated en masse
root_causes: Identity Provider (Auth0/Okta/Keycloak) rotated private signing key without downstream JWKS cache invalidation
Microservice JWKS client caching outdated public key kid with zero TTL fallback
Clock skew between Auth server and API gateway exceeding token leeway (nbf/exp)
mitigation_steps: Trigger manual cache flush on API gateway JWKS client cache: POST /admin/internal/jwks/flush-cache
Verify that the new kid in the incoming JWT matches the published keys in jwks.json
If identity provider rotation failed, revert the active signing key ID in the auth management console
long_term_fix: Implement resilient JWKS cache-on-demand fetching when an unknown kid is encountered with strict rate limiting.

title: Credential Stuffing & Distributed Brute-Force Attack
symptoms: Astronomical surge in POST /api/v1/auth/login attempts from residential proxies
Failure rate of login attempts spiking from normal 4% to 92%
WAF (Cloudflare/AWS WAF) anomaly alert triggered on rate limit thresholds
High CPU load on bcrypt password hashing workers in Auth service
root_causes: Compromised credential database combo-list dumped online being tested against public auth endpoints
Lack of IP-reputation and CAPTCHA challenge on repeated bad credentials
diagnostic_commands: aws wafv2 get-sampled-requests --web-acl-arn <ARN> --rule-metric-name LoginRateLimit --scope CLOUDFRONT --time-window StartTime=...,EndTime=... --max-items 50
kubectl logs -l app=auth-service --tail=200 | grep 'login_failed' | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -20
mitigation_steps: Enable Cloudflare 'Under Attack' mode or tighten WAF IP rate limit rule on /auth/login to 5 req/min per IP
Enforce mandatory Turnstile / reCAPTCHA challenge on the login endpoint
Lock accounts exhibiting >10 consecutive failed attempts and notify users to reset passwords
long_term_fix: Integrate HaveIBeenPwned password breach check and deploy bot management with machine learning behavioral scoring.

title: Kubernetes Pod OOMKilled (Out of Memory) CrashLoop
symptoms: Pods in CrashLoopBackOff with Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137
Service capacity degraded causing 503 Service Unavailable / 504 Gateway Timeout
Prometheus alert: KubePodCrashLooping & ContainerMemoryUsageTooHigh
HPA flapping or failing to spin up healthy replicas in time
root_causes: Container memory limit (resources.limits.memory) set too tight for incoming traffic spike
Unbounded in-memory queue or caching without eviction policy
JVM / Node heap size configured higher than container cgroup limit
diagnostic_commands: kubectl get pods -n production -l app=<SERVICE_NAME> -o wide
kubectl describe pod <POD_NAME> -n production | grep -A 5 -B 2 OOMKilled
mitigation_steps: Bump container memory limits in deployment spec: kubectl set resources deployment <DEPLOYMENT_NAME> -n production --limits=memory=2Gi,cpu=1000m
Scale up deployment replica count to distribute memory load: kubectl scale deployment <DEPLOYMENT_NAME> -n production --replicas=10
Restart failing deployment to reclaim leaked memory: kubectl rollout restart deployment <DEPLOYMENT_NAME> -n production
long_term_fix: Profile heap dump with Chrome DevTools/JProfiler, fix memory leak, and configure Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA).

title: Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) Disk Space Exhaustion
symptoms: StatefulSet pods crashing with 'No space left on device' (ENOSPC)
Database or Kafka/Elasticsearch broker refusing writes
Prometheus alert: DiskSpaceFillingUp (Predict1HourRemaining)
Read-only filesystem error mounted on /var/data
root_causes: Unrotated log files accumulating in container volume
Elasticsearch index retention policy not trimming old indices
Unexpected write surge without volume autoscaling
diagnostic_commands: kubectl exec -it <POD_NAME> -n production -- du -sh /var/data/* | sort -rh | head -10
mitigation_steps: Trigger immediate volume expansion: edit PVC storage spec from 100Gi to 200Gi (if storage class supports VolumeExpansion)
Clean up old archived logs and temporary files: kubectl exec -it <POD_NAME> -n production -- find /var/log -name '*.gz' -mtime +7 -delete
For Elasticsearch/Kafka, execute index curator to drop oldest snapshots/topics
long_term_fix: Implement automated storage retention policies and configure volume expansion alerts at 75% threshold.

title: Upstream Gateway Timeout and Cascading Circuit Breaker Trips
symptoms: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout and 503 Service Unavailable spikes on Edge API Gateway
Circuit breaker state transitioned to OPEN for downstream checkout-service
Thread pool exhaustion in Kong / Envoy / Express gateway
Customer checkout completion rate dropping to near zero
root_causes: Downstream microservice experiencing latency degradation due to database lock contention
Absence of deadline propagation / aggressive client retry storms without exponential backoff
Thread pool queue overflowing in the API gateway
diagnostic_commands: kubectl logs -l app=api-gateway -n production --tail=200 | grep 'upstream request timeout'
mitigation_steps: Enable circuit breaker fallback response (cached/degraded mode) to shed load from failing downstream service
Scale up downstream service replicas to process queued requests: kubectl scale deployment checkout-service -n production --replicas=15
Temporarily drop client retry storm at gateway layer by rejecting retried idempotent headers with HTTP 429
long_term_fix: Implement strict distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry, gRPC/HTTP deadline budgets, and exponential backoff with jitter.

title: Redis Cache Cache Stampede and Connection Saturations
symptoms: Redis CPU utilization hitting 100% on primary node
Sudden flood of DB queries for hot cached keys (e.g. homepage categories / configuration)
Redis error: ERR max number of clients reached (maxclients)
P99 latency of API services jumping from 25ms to 3200ms
root_causes: High-traffic cache key expired without probabilistic early recomputation (cache stampede / thundering herd)
Unbounded Redis keyspace without maxmemory eviction policy (volatile-lru)
Microservice instances opening new Redis connections on every request instead of connection pool reuse
diagnostic_commands: redis-cli -h redis-cluster.prod info clients | grep connected_clients
mitigation_steps: Manually warm and set high-traffic expired cache key with extended TTL: redis-cli -h redis-cluster.prod SET <HOT_KEY> <VALUE> EX 86400
Activate mutex locking (single-flight) in the backend to ensure only 1 worker computes cache misses
Increase maxclients on Redis node: redis-cli -h redis-cluster.prod CONFIG SET maxclients 20000
long_term_fix: Add XFetch / probabilistic early expiration to all hot keys and use client-side caching (Redis RESP3).

title: Payment Webhook Failure and Signature Verification Mismatch
symptoms: Stripe/Adyen webhook dashboard showing 100% 400 Bad Request delivery failures
Customer subscriptions not activating after successful credit card charge
Application log: StripeSignatureVerificationError: No signatures found matching the expected signature for payload
Order status stuck in 'payment_pending' state
root_causes: Stripe webhook signing secret rotated in merchant dashboard without updating backend env var STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
Express body-parser middleware parsing JSON before raw body verification, mutating payload bytes
Reverse proxy stripping or modifying Stripe-Signature HTTP header
diagnostic_commands: kubectl get secret payment-secrets -n production -o jsonpath='{.data.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET}' | base64 --decode
mitigation_steps: Retrieve active signing secret from Stripe Dashboard -> Developers -> Webhooks and update Kubernetes secret
Trigger rolling update of payment service: kubectl rollout restart deployment payment-service -n production
Replay failed webhook events from Stripe dashboard CLI once verification is restored: stripe events resend <EVENT_ID>
long_term_fix: Use automated secret synchronization from AWS Secrets Manager / HashiCorp Vault with zero-downtime dual-secret support.

title: Frontend Single Page App Chunk Loading Error
symptoms: ChunkLoadError: Loading chunk 842 failed (missing: https://cdn.company.com/assets/842.a9f4c.js)
Users seeing blank white screen of death or broken routing navigation
Sentry / Datadog RUM reporting 10,000+ ChunkLoadError events following new frontend release
Edge CDN returning 404 Not Found on hashed JavaScript chunks
root_causes: New frontend deployment purged older hashed chunks from S3/GCS bucket before users with older index.html reloaded
CDN edge cache purging delay causing partial cache miss on newer asset bundles
mitigation_steps: Restore previous build's /assets folder back to S3 bucket without overwriting index.html so both versions coexist
Trigger fast CDN cache invalidation for /*: aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id <DIST_ID> --paths '/*'
Deploy window.addEventListener('error') script in index.html to force one-time auto-reload on ChunkLoadError
long_term_fix: Configure asset pipeline with immutable S3 storage retention (keep historical chunks for 30 days) and dynamic lazy retry wrapper.

title: CoreDNS Resolution Failures and Service Discovery Breakdown
symptoms: Internal service-to-service calls failing with 'dial tcp: lookup order-service.production.svc.cluster.local: i/o timeout'
Pods unable to resolve external domains (e.g. api.stripe.com, api.datadog.com)
Prometheus alert: CoreDNSLatencyHigh / CoreDNSErrorsHigh
Cascading 500 errors across all microservice boundaries
root_causes: CoreDNS deployment under-provisioned for cluster query rate (exhausting 1000m CPU limit)
Conntrack table saturation on worker nodes causing UDP packet drops for DNS queries (port 53)
ndots:5 default in resolv.conf generating 5 redundant DNS queries per lookup
mitigation_steps: Scale up CoreDNS replicas immediately: kubectl scale deployment coredns -n kube-system --replicas=8
Deploy NodeLocal DNSCache daemonset to intercept DNS queries locally on node loopback
Increase nf_conntrack_max sysctl on worker nodes if table saturation is detected
long_term_fix: Implement NodeLocal DNSCache cluster-wide and configure Autopath in CoreDNS configmap.

title: TLS/mTLS Certificate Expiration and Auto-Renewal Failure
symptoms: Cert-manager warning: Internal mTLS leaf certificate will expire
Auto-renewal failed due to DNS challenge timeout
Certificate lifecycle alert: cert expiring within threshold
SSL handshake failure: certificate has expired (x509: certificate signed by unknown authority)
root_causes: Cert-manager Let's Encrypt / Vault DNS01 challenge webhook timing out
ACME challenge token propagation delay on authoritative nameserver
Stale ClusterIssuer credentials or expired IAM role for Route53/Cloud DNS
mitigation_steps: Trigger manual cert renewal: kubectl cert-manager renew <CERTIFICATE_NAME> -n production
Verify DNS01 challenge TXT record propagation via dig @8.8.8.8 _acme-challenge.<DOMAIN> TXT
If automated challenge is broken, issue emergency 90-day self-signed or internal CA certificate
long_term_fix: Set up Prometheus alert rule at 14 days before certificate expiration and configure HTTP-01 challenge fallback.

title: Payment Idempotency Key Conflicts and Concurrency Collisions
symptoms: Payment API surge in 409 Conflict responses
Idempotency-Key collision on checkout purchase submissions
Users experiencing double-click checkout errors
Log: Idempotency conflict: simultaneous requests with identical key in-flight
root_causes: Frontend checkout button not disabled immediately upon initial click submission
Aggressive client-side HTTP timeout retry submitting identical idempotency key before worker lock release
Distributed redis lock duration on idempotency keys set too short
diagnostic_commands: kubectl logs -l app=payment-service -n production --tail=200 | grep '409 Conflict'
mitigation_steps: Deploy hotfix to debounce checkout button in web & mobile clients (disable button on click)
Return HTTP 425 Too Early or poll status URL instead of immediate hard 409 error
Adjust idempotency lock TTL in payment-service config from 3s to 15s
long_term_fix: Standardize IETF Idempotency-Key draft specifications across mobile and web checkout flows.

title: Deprecated API Endpoint Sunset and Migration Enforcement
symptoms: Clients calling deprecated /api/v1 endpoint instead of /api/v2
Sunset header telemetry logging high volume on legacy routes
Recommendation API deprecation notices in gateway metrics
Downstream v1 payload schema parsing overhead
root_causes: Legacy mobile client app versions have not been forced to update
Third-party partner integrations still pointing to v1 URL routes
Lack of progressive rate-limiting or artificial latency degradation on deprecated routes
diagnostic_commands: SELECT user_agent, count(*) FROM api_access_logs WHERE path LIKE '/api/v1/%' GROUP BY user_agent ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10;
mitigation_steps: Verify that Sunset and Deprecation HTTP headers are correctly returned with RFC 8594 compliance
Send migration reminder notifications to partner developers identifying top caller IPs
Schedule brownout test (introduce 500ms artificial latency on v1) to incentivize upgrade
long_term_fix: Enforce minimum supported mobile app build version and establish automated API retirement policy.

title: Edge CDN Ingress Transit Latency and Regional POP Degradation
symptoms: Elevated edge ingress latency in specific region (e.g. US-West)
Cloudflare/Fastly reporting increased TTFB transit between POP and origin
ISP fiber cut or peering congestion impacting edge traffic
User interactive latency degraded in Pacific Northwest
root_causes: Upstream Tier 1 transit provider experiencing fiber cut / subsea cable maintenance
BGP Anycast routing suboptimal routes to origin datacenters
Edge origin health check threshold flapping
mitigation_steps: Reroute Cloudflare edge ingress traffic from congested POP to neighboring healthy POP (e.g. Portland -> San Jose)
Enable Cloudflare Argo Smart Routing to bypass congested transit backbones
Increase origin keep-alive timeout on edge reverse proxies
long_term_fix: Deploy multi-cloud dual-origin redundancy with automated latency-based BGP steering.
